scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A damaged but salvageable MOU survives after Qatar/Oman mediation. Iran stops further attacks, US strikes remain limited, and monitored corridors reopen in phases. Brent holds $72-82/bbl as shipping resumes unevenly and Ras Laffan recovery remains late-August at best. Probability cut to 45% after renewed tanker attacks, US strikes and oil-waiver revocation.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Repeated MOU breach claims keep Hormuz traffic constrained. Iran insists on Tehran-approved routes; US/UK/French patrols expand; insurers price high-risk transit. Brent trades $78-95/bbl, JKM holds $18-22/MMBtu, iTraxx Asia IG widens toward 145bp, and ASEAN importers hedge freight and fuel exposure.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Retaliation cycle resumes. Iran attacks or seizes more vessels, US strikes broaden, and the MOU collapses before nuclear talks progress. Hormuz is re-militarised; Brent spikes $115-140/bbl and LNG risk premia surge. Probability raised to 20% after three vessel attacks and direct US strikes around the strait.
